NA-AUTH-001.title: Signer/predecessor confusion enables confused-deputy calls
NA-AUTH-001.activation: composable public methods authorize or pay `signer_account_id`, or self-callbacks infer the original user from predecessor.

NA-AUTH-002.title: Exposed privileged/internal endpoint
NA-AUTH-002.activation: missing/ignored role check, unprotected `#[private]` path, public test helper, user-controlled authority argument, an internal or trait implementation annotated with `#[near]`/`#[near_bindgen]` exports a helper that bypasses its guarded wrapper, initialization/ownership/admin transitions do not follow one explicit caller-and-role policy, or revocation/renunciation can remove the final principal needed for pause, upgrade, recovery, or another documented critical operation.

NA-AUTH-003.title: One-yocto or function-call-key boundary is unsafe
NA-AUTH-003.activation: a sensitive exported method is nonpayable, omits exact `assert_one_yocto()`/equivalent validation, accepts zero or arbitrary deposit, or remains callable through a compromised third-party function-call key without the intended wallet-confirmation boundary.

NA-AUTH-004.title: Stale access key bypasses new governance
NA-AUTH-004.activation: ownership changes without rotating full-access/function-call keys, keys cannot be removed, or fallback keys bypass delay/multisig.

NA-AUTH-005.title: Initialization is public, repeatable, or binds unsafe first state
NA-AUTH-005.activation: initializer is exported without `#[init]`/state-existence protection, `ignore_state` is reachable, first caller selects owner, or role/config/account relationships are not validated.

NA-AUTH-006.title: Effective upgrade authority bypasses governance
NA-AUTH-006.activation: self-upgrade, full-access key, owner plugin, or staged code bypasses multisig/timelock.

NA-AUTH-007.title: Signed intent replay, recomposition, or weak domain binding
NA-AUTH-007.activation: failed bundles leave replayable sub-intents, nonce consumption is late, a purpose/type discriminator or other domain field is absent, two accepted message schemas can encode the same signed bytes/hash for different privileged actions, or key state is unbounded.

NA-AUTH-008.title: Passkey/solver verification accepts attacker-controlled context
NA-AUTH-008.activation: Passkey assertions, device registration, or solver quotes accepted by a value-bearing path

NA-AUTH-009.title: Separate caller, originator, payer, and beneficiary
NA-AUTH-009.activation: Calls can be forwarded or delegated; A later credit or authorization uses one identity in place of another

NA-AUTH-010.title: Check privileged methods against limited credentials
NA-AUTH-010.activation: A credential may invoke only selected methods or low-friction actions; A privileged state change may be reachable with that credential

NA-AUTH-011.title: Bind initialization to deployment authority
NA-AUTH-011.activation: A newly deployed object needs one-time initialization; An untrusted actor may reach it before initialization completes

NA-ASYNC-001.title: Late reservation enables split-receipt double spend
NA-ASYNC-001.activation: a method checks available state, emits a promise, and only debits/locks/consumes in a callback.

NA-ASYNC-002.title: Missing or incomplete failure compensation
NA-ASYNC-002.activation: state changes before a promise and no complete callback handles failure, malformed return, or low gas.

NA-ASYNC-003.title: Callback authority or identity mismatch
NA-ASYNC-003.activation: a callback/resolver/migrate/internal endpoint lacks `#[private]`, trusts callback arguments or injected promise results as caller authentication, or uses predecessor as the original user.

NA-ASYNC-004.title: Promise graph or return semantics are misinterpreted
NA-ASYNC-004.activation: wrong or unchecked `promise_results_count`, wrong `promise_result` index, missing `and/then`, no returned terminal promise, unchecked `PromiseResult` bytes, top-level execution success is treated as business success, a proof/event/authorization is consumed before every required downstream effect succeeds, or settlement applies a fee, route, oracle bound, protocol version, or external configuration that changed after the initiating receipt without binding the user's accepted bounds.

NA-ASYNC-005.title: Pending state can be permanently poisoned
NA-ASYNC-005.activation: lock is set before unbounded work, log/serialization, low-gas callback, yield, or external dependency.

NA-ASYNC-006.title: Stale callback snapshot overwrites intervening state
NA-ASYNC-006.activation: an initiating receipt serializes a mutable struct or derived share/rate value into callback arguments and the callback later writes it back after another receipt can mutate the same record.

NA-ASYNC-007.title: A foreign operation releases or extends another operation's lock
NA-ASYNC-007.activation: a shared boolean lock has no operation token; a public ping/retry or unrelated callback unconditionally calls `unlock`; or a later user's action refreshes a shared deadline that governs earlier pending withdrawals.

NA-ASYNC-008.title: Resumable cursor is not bound to operation context
NA-ASYNC-008.activation: a public method stores one shared iterator/cursor but accepts the recipient, transfer-versus-recovery mode, filter, limit, or asset again on later calls; initial-only validation is skipped on resume; or concurrent callers can advance or replace the same checkpoint.

NA-ASYNC-009.title: Resolver refund/ownership semantics break conservation
NA-ASYNC-009.activation: resolver public, malformed result unchecked, FT failure does not attempt full refund, FT refund is not capped by both the original transfer and receiver's current balance, actual-spent return polarity is inverted, an NFT resolver overwrites an intervening retransfer/burn, mirrors are not restored, NFT approval mutation is not restricted to the current owner, an approved transfer accepts a stale/mismatched supplied `approval_id`, re-approval reuses an ID, transfer fails to clear approvals, approval notification failure is incorrectly treated as rollback, or a bridge/escrow consumes its proof/nonce and marks settlement terminal before learning the actual amount used versus refunded by `ft_transfer_call`.

NA-ASYNC-010.title: Reserve capacity before concurrent work
NA-ASYNC-010.activation: A bounded resource is checked before allocation; Another operation can pass the check before the first allocation commits

NA-ASYNC-011.title: Recover when the effect commits but bookkeeping fails
NA-ASYNC-011.activation: The business effect and local accounting can commit independently; The accounting step can fail after the effect

NA-ASYNC-012.title: Separate transport success from business completion
NA-ASYNC-012.activation: Completion depends on an external or deferred result; The interface can fail, return malformed data, or report partial work

NA-ASYNC-013.title: Define authority across dependency rotation
NA-ASYNC-013.activation: Work is dispatched to a trusted dependency; Its identity or authority can change before the result is applied

NA-ASYNC-014.title: Count logical work once across retries
NA-ASYNC-014.activation: A logical operation can be retried; A derived counter can commit independently of its business outcome

NA-ASYNC-015.title: Preserve entitlement after partial completion
NA-ASYNC-015.activation: A downstream operation can accept part of an input; Returned or unused value is held by an intermediary

NA-ASYNC-016.title: Serialize or deduplicate overlapping bulk operations
NA-ASYNC-016.activation: An authorized bulk operation has deferred effects; Another invocation can begin before completion is recorded

NA-ASYNC-017.title: Recover when cancellation itself expires or fails
NA-ASYNC-017.activation: An operation reserves resources; Its cancellation or replacement is a separate operation that can become unusable

NA-ACCOUNT-001.title: Global storage delta is charged to the wrong account
NA-ACCOUNT-001.activation: per-user accounting compares current whole-contract `env::storage_usage()` with a user baseline, spans an external/interleaved operation, or assigns another account's growth during liquidation/cleanup.

NA-ACCOUNT-002.title: Liability, reserve, fee, or supply accounting is inconsistent
NA-ACCOUNT-002.activation: raw account balance is used as deposits, refundable depositor principal also funds storage or rewards, time-based rewards are not bounded by earned fees or a separately funded reserve, balances are sampled after untrusted calls, an adapter or external market can report assets/proceeds without reconciliation to observed token deltas or a bounded authoritative source, protocol or a shared relayer account subsidizes caller-controlled attached deposits/fees (including repeated one-yocto child calls), paths omit a ledger update or external transfer, a terminal fee can be bypassed by leaving dust, or a caller-controlled list charges/burns/consumes an entitlement once while granting a payout, mint, vote, claim, refund, or other benefit per occurrence.

NA-ACCOUNT-003.title: Accumulated value has no safe claim or recovery transition
NA-ACCOUNT-003.activation: value accrues in state or contract balance but no exported method can release it, the only recipient can become unregistered, or emergency/pause states disable recovery permanently.

NA-ACCOUNT-004.title: Accrual or reward snapshot is not settled before mutation
NA-ACCOUNT-004.activation: rate/weight/config/position changes do not call the relevant accrue/snapshot function for every affected asset and account, or a time-chunk/snapshot design accounts only finalized periods so borrowing, repaying, supplying, withdrawing, liquidating, or changing collateral within the open period receives free time or loses earned value.

NA-ACCOUNT-005.title: Vault share conversion or managed-asset accounting dilutes claimants
NA-ACCOUNT-005.activation: the first depositor or a direct donor can manipulate price-per-share; zero-share deposits are accepted; paid-out versus required amounts use the wrong rounding direction; `total_assets` omits direct donations or trusts mutable adapter-reported values without balance-delta/bounded reconciliation; a positional market-to-adapter mapping can silently change after reordering; virtual offsets, underlying asset identity, or conversion basis can change after capitalization; preview/max results omit limits or fees; or async withdrawal burns/finalizes shares without an operation-bound rollback/recovery path.

NA-ACCOUNT-006.title: Preserve recovery when the primary operation is rejected
NA-ACCOUNT-006.activation: The system already controls a user's resource; A policy threshold rejects normal processing while consuming an admission marker

NA-ACCOUNT-007.title: Assign all residual value after allocation
NA-ACCOUNT-007.activation: An allocation leaves a remainder after requested outputs and costs; The remainder can become unowned or inaccessible

NA-STATE-001.title: Coupled indexes or lifecycle state diverge
NA-STATE-001.activation: one path updates a primary map but not secondary index, manual token/NFT transfer bypasses protocol mirrors, two logical roles such as sender/receiver resolve to the same storage key and independently computed stale snapshots are written sequentially, code mutates an owned/deserialized value returned by a legacy `near_sdk::collections` lookup without reinserting/replacing it in the collection, a destructive full-object replacement silently erases fields that should survive, or an in-flight sale, bid, bond, liquidation, promise, or queue entry references an object that another public path can merge, delete, replace, or renumber before settlement.

NA-STATE-002.title: Getter or validation path mutates/creates state
NA-STATE-002.activation: `or_insert`/lazy initialization appears in getters, checks, or rejected paths, or a read-like method uses `Option::take`, legacy `LazyOption::take`, or an equivalent destructive accessor and unintentionally replaces/removes live state.

NA-STATE-003.title: Migration corrupts or strands persistent state
NA-STATE-003.activation: no versioning/migration, wrong old struct, public/repeatable migration, unbounded migration, or orphaned state.

NA-STATE-004.title: Missing state-machine transition or validation bypass
NA-STATE-004.activation: missing, inconsistent, or bypassable lifecycle checks govern pause/denylist, roles, amounts, deadlines, batches, liquidation, recovery, or dependent configuration; an input can also become unusable after costs or transformations.

NA-STATE-005.title: Check individual allocation as well as aggregate totals
NA-STATE-005.activation: A supplied list determines allocations; Validation checks aggregate totals without establishing unique complete membership

NA-STATE-006.title: Reconcile mutations during snapshot migration
NA-STATE-006.activation: A snapshot is copied to a new representation; The old representation can change before cutover

NA-STATE-007.title: Prove resource amplification before reporting missing limits
NA-STATE-007.activation: Users can request resource-consuming work; A proposed finding depends on aggregate demand or missing quotas

NA-STATE-008.title: Distinguish optional restrictions from required permissions
NA-STATE-008.activation: Membership and restriction configuration have independent lifecycles; An absent rule has defined policy semantics

NA-STATE-009.title: Clean every losing attempt after a winner completes
NA-STATE-009.activation: Several attempts represent one logical operation; Attempts occupy different states and share quota or indexes

NA-STATE-010.title: Preserve decision semantics when bounded history changes
NA-STATE-010.activation: Security or risk decisions rely on bounded historical data; Resizing or eviction can change the meaning of missing entries

NA-STATE-011.title: Validate collection cardinality before per-item checks
NA-STATE-011.activation: A nonempty collection is required for a valid operation; A path relies only on checks applied to each member

NA-STATE-012.title: Preserve rights across provisional-to-final transitions
NA-STATE-012.activation: A provisional operation coexists with a paid or time-dependent recovery claim; Finalization deletes or overwrites that claim

NA-STATE-013.title: Validate destinations before committing to delivery
NA-STATE-013.activation: A user supplies a destination for later recovery or delivery; The system stores or charges for it before validating usability

NA-STATE-014.title: Make optimistic approval assumptions explicit
NA-STATE-014.activation: An action becomes executable unless a reviewer vetoes it; Its safety depends on timely review rather than fully automated validity

NA-STATE-015.title: Keep replay protection compatible with recovery
NA-STATE-015.activation: Cleanup deletes an operation or recovery record; A consumed marker survives and blocks every legitimate retry

NA-STATE-016.title: Validate configuration combinations
NA-STATE-016.activation: Several settings jointly determine an operational invariant; Individual type checks allow incompatible combinations

NA-ECON-001.title: Asset identity, unit, or collateral type is confused
NA-ECON-001.activation: generic tuples/strings or shared maps let collateral types merge, code assumes underlying equals collateral, global liquidity substitutes for asset-specific liquidity, chain-specific recipient/address encodings are accepted under the wrong chain kind, or logs/metadata disagree with execution.

NA-ECON-002.title: Rounding, precision, overflow, or unit error changes value
NA-ECON-002.activation: division precedes multiplication, `f32`/`f64` or float-derived configuration participates in monetary accounting, APY/unit semantics are ambiguous, intermediates overflow, casts truncate, decimal scaling or exponentiation can panic or underflow a nonzero value to zero, caps disagree, or an increase/decrease delta subtracts operands in the wrong direction and permanently reverts or credits the wrong amount.

NA-ECON-003.title: Public input, reveal, reward, or randomness can be ordered, copied, or biased
NA-ECON-003.activation: challenge/proof/reveal/answer/solution data is public before inclusion and the first valid submitter receives value or changes exclusive state; a permissionless finalization/signing call lets the transaction sender choose an unbound fee beneficiary that a copier can replace; auctions, first-come mints/claims, or trades expose predictable price impact; or `env::random_seed()` influences material value while the producer for that block can predict the seed and choose matching inputs, transaction order/inclusion, or whether to include a later resolve. The seed's deterministic/verifiable derivation does not remove this producer advantage.

NA-ECON-004.title: Bind compensation to the original resource generation
NA-ECON-004.activation: An operation can settle or compensate later; A configured resource can be replaced while it is pending

NA-RESOURCE-001.title: Attacker-induced storage is unpaid or underpriced
NA-RESOURCE-001.activation: public/hook methods grow state for free, use constants/partial key sizes, subsidize third-party storage deposits, let a caller choose a fee or deposit charged to a shared relayer/storage account, permit Sybil records, or let an attacker repeat individually cheap writes whose storage stake is borne disproportionately by the contract.

NA-RESOURCE-002.title: Persistent prefix collision or orphaned nested state
NA-RESOURCE-002.activation: raw string concatenation, timestamp/height uniqueness, reused enum prefix, or removal of a parent record/collection handle without deleting the child collection's prefixed raw keys.

NA-RESOURCE-003.title: Detached SDK collection loses metadata or aliases state
NA-RESOURCE-003.activation: a method constructs `Vector`, `LookupMap`, `UnorderedMap`, `IterableMap`, `LookupSet`, `Lazy`, `LazyOption`, or a similar collection locally with an existing/raw prefix; modifies it without persisting its metadata; or prevents a `near_sdk::store` value from running its version-specific `Drop`/`flush` path through `mem::forget`, static retention, or equivalent control flow.

NA-RESOURCE-004.title: Native root collection bloats `STATE` and bricks execution
NA-RESOURCE-004.activation: contract state contains attacker-growable native `Vec`, `HashMap`, `HashSet`, `BTreeMap`, `String`, or nested native collections instead of SDK persistent collections.

NA-RESOURCE-005.title: Unbounded work, logs, or state serialization blocks core operations
NA-RESOURCE-005.activation: unbounded args/collections, root native collections, unnecessarily iterable/ordered structures, batch iteration, large logs or JSON/Borsh payloads, repeated full serialization, stale gas constants, callback gas starvation, or approval/state admission can grow beyond what a mandatory future revoke/unregister/cleanup operation can process.

NA-RESOURCE-006.title: Make mandatory bulk work bounded and resumable
NA-RESOURCE-006.activation: A required operation processes a growing population in one execution; Smaller independent executions cannot satisfy its global completion check

NA-RESOURCE-007.title: Assign every accepted surplus to a payer and policy
NA-RESOURCE-007.activation: Admission accepts more than a required amount; Success or failure accounts for only the required portion

NA-RESOURCE-008.title: Budget repeated variable-length payloads
NA-RESOURCE-008.activation: User-influenced variable-length data is persisted; One logical object is copied into multiple records or responses

NA-RESOURCE-009.title: Account for old records in new pricing paths
NA-RESOURCE-009.activation: Creation or copying consumes metered resources; Legacy objects were stored under a different charging rule

NA-RESOURCE-010.title: Make sponsorship and refund attribution explicit
NA-RESOURCE-010.activation: One principal funds setup or registration for another; The beneficiary may later withdraw or reclaim the funding

NA-INTEGRATION-001.title: Receiver hook trusts the wrong token or sender context
NA-INTEGRATION-001.activation: an FT hook accepts a counterfeit predecessor, an NFT hook treats `sender_id` as `previous_owner_id` even though an approved operator can make them differ, or free-form `msg` selects an unvalidated asset, beneficiary, route, or action.

NA-INTEGRATION-002.title: Standard ABI or lifecycle semantics drift breaks interoperability
NA-INTEGRATION-002.activation: any NEP in the pinned registry is claimed, exported, activated, implemented, or materially depended upon and its exact behavior differs. Examples include signature/serializer/numeric representation drift; optional/default or panic/`false`/`null` mismatch; wrong return polarity; missing ABI; deposit-rule conflict; lifecycle ordering drift; unsupported peer assumptions; NEP-145 beneficiary/payer/refund confusion or withdrawal without value transfer; NEP-171/178 approval-ID representation; wallet/signature domain mismatch; host-function ABI/result confusion; or node/runtime activation/state-transition disagreement.

NA-INTEGRATION-003.title: Finality, proof, or timeout races release value twice
NA-INTEGRATION-003.activation: proof and timeout/unlock can race, a nonce/proof is consumed too early or too late relative to terminal downstream success, source confirmations are weak, a sequence/reset is not scoped to the configured emitter, security-relevant header/event metadata is omitted from the canonical proof identity, or a callback is not idempotent.

NA-INTEGRATION-004.title: Valid proof is accepted from an untrusted emitter or route
NA-INTEGRATION-004.activation: proof verification establishes inclusion/finality but the consumer accepts an attacker-deployed contract's otherwise valid event, trusts an emitter supplied inside the proof payload, or mutates token/address mappings before comparing the event origin with the configured per-chain factory/locker.

NA-INTEGRATION-005.title: Stale, manipulable, or unavailable input corrupts decisions
NA-INTEGRATION-005.activation: a price/reward/rate lacks freshness, decimals, source authentication, fallback, or manipulation bounds; or a confidence interval is applied in the wrong direction or without a policy bound so uncertainty itself triggers unsafe liquidation or borrowing.

NA-INTEGRATION-006.title: Validate the result after costs and transformations
NA-INTEGRATION-006.activation: An input loses value or capacity through fees or transformations; A downstream system imposes a minimum usable result

NA-INTEGRATION-007.title: Verify meaning and authorization before shared commitment
NA-INTEGRATION-007.activation: Untrusted structured data can reserve shared resources; Parsing does not establish all required semantic or authorization predicates

NA-INTEGRATION-008.title: Distinguish accepted state from usable resources
NA-INTEGRATION-008.activation: An upstream system accepts or records a resource; Independent rules govern when that resource may be consumed

NA-CRYPTO-001.title: Ambiguous, non-canonical, or incomplete decoding changes authority or execution
NA-CRYPTO-001.activation: custom delimiter parsing is context-free, a decoder accepts trailing bytes, nested values can inject actions, external IDs have inconsistent case normalization, security-sensitive account fields remain unvalidated strings, or a compact/custom AccountId representation is not injective, canonical, length-bounded, and exactly reversible.

NA-CRYPTO-002.title: Threshold request, participant, transcript, or response is not cryptographically bound
NA-CRYPTO-002.activation: peer IDs are accepted without unique asset-to-network binding; vector position is confused with participant index; a coordinator can choose unchecked derivation data; a response handler accepts a caller or `payload_hash` not bound to the pending request; or two operation purposes share the same transcript/signature domain.

NA-CRYPTO-003.title: Threshold, quorum, corruption, or resharing assumptions disagree across phases
NA-CRYPTO-003.activation: signing threshold differs from reliable-broadcast corruption bounds; `threshold = 1`, changed membership, or changed threshold reaches an untested/invalid branch; a coordinator waits for every participant despite a threshold protocol; or `>= threshold` early responses can override a contrary honest majority.

NA-CRYPTO-004.title: Presignature reuse across split views leaks the signing key
NA-CRYPTO-004.activation: disjoint or equivocating signer views can select the same presignature for different messages, tweaks, or participant subsets; presignature consumption is tracked only locally; or participant-count/index bounds permit overlapping threshold groups to complete inconsistent sessions.

NA-CRYPTO-005.title: Secret material survives or crosses an unsafe operational boundary
NA-CRYPTO-005.activation: secrets are passed on command lines, persisted in CI/container artifacts, retained after DKG/resharing, stored with excessive permissions, or left in ordinary buffers without a deliberate zeroization/threat-model decision.

NA-CRYPTO-006.title: Encryption nonce, context binding, or key derivation is unsafe
NA-CRYPTO-006.activation: AES-GCM or another nonce-sensitive AEAD repeats a nonce; encrypted database values can be swapped between keys/records because AAD omits identity; a raw hash substitutes for a required KDF; or ciphertext/version/key-rotation context is ambiguous.

NA-CRYPTO-007.title: Attestation does not bind the claimed platform, TCB, measurement, and runtime configuration
NA-CRYPTO-007.activation: TCB status is ignored; environment parsing/tagging changes what was measured or claimed; privileged container/runtime configuration lies outside the attested boundary; or attestation proves code but not the key/configuration used for MPC/CKD decisions.

NA-CRYPTO-008.title: Treat deletion and authority revocation separately
NA-CRYPTO-008.activation: An operation creates externally usable authority; Local rejection or deletion can occur after that authority exists

NA-RUNTIME-001.title: Untrusted host/runtime work can panic, allocate, or execute before proportional charging
NA-RUNTIME-001.activation: gas is deducted after allocation/read/serialization; lengths or multiplication overflow before a bound; attacker-controlled receipt/account/Wasm data drives large allocation; deserialization or storage imports panic; or runtime backends/architectures disagree on accepted input or result.

NA-RUNTIME-002.title: Block production, fork choice, finalization, or validator-set transitions violate agreement/liveness
NA-RUNTIME-002.activation: producer scheduling can be sped up/manipulated, block acceptance enables systematic censorship, validator removal/update crashes or diverges, mutable process state substitutes for consensus state, or finalization logic permits conflicting forks.

NA-OFFCHAIN-001.title: Indexer trusts failed, foreign, or malformed chain data
NA-OFFCHAIN-001.activation: substring contract match, tx acceptance without receipt checks, untrusted decode with panic, optimistic data used for irreversible payout, or failed outcome args/logs are ingested.

NA-OFFCHAIN-002.title: Relayer retry, persistence, or nonce ordering loses/doubles funds
NA-OFFCHAIN-002.activation: pub/sub loss, Redis/DB outage, send-before-persist, parallel access-key nonces, retry without event identity, or ABI parameter drift.

NA-OFFCHAIN-003.title: Unsafe off-chain input or authorization reaches a dangerous sink
NA-OFFCHAIN-003.activation: string-interpolated SQL, source/client-side password authorization, unsafe callback URL, public mutation route, or production mock/test endpoint.

NA-OFFCHAIN-004.title: Dependency/build/release configuration changes security semantics
NA-OFFCHAIN-004.activation: dependency, macro, toolchain, feature, release-profile, or deployment inputs can change security-relevant build or runtime behavior.

NA-OFFCHAIN-005.title: Missing or incomplete security tests
NA-OFFCHAIN-005.activation: tests omit material lifecycle, failure, authorization, or boundary scenarios, or use mocks with different production semantics.

NA-OFFCHAIN-006.title: Missing or inconsistent security observability
NA-OFFCHAIN-006.activation: security-relevant events or diagnostics are absent, inconsistent with committed state, or insufficient to distinguish actionable bounded failures.

NA-OFFCHAIN-007.title: Documentation or specification is incomplete
NA-OFFCHAIN-007.activation: documentation or operational assumptions disagree with actual entrypoints, authority, units, receipt outcomes, policy, or recovery.

NA-OFFCHAIN-008.title: Non-material code quality or efficiency issue
NA-OFFCHAIN-008.activation: The named target behavior exists and can be reached by an attacker.

NA-OFFCHAIN-009.title: Bind release artifacts to reviewed inputs
NA-OFFCHAIN-009.activation: Deployment or release tooling consumes external tools or mutable build inputs; Those inputs can affect shipped artifacts

NA-OFFCHAIN-010.title: Expose useful diagnostics without removing bounds
NA-OFFCHAIN-010.activation: Responses or operations have intentional bounds; Failures do not expose enough information for correct recovery

NA-OFFCHAIN-011.title: Distinguish validity deadlines from observation deadlines
NA-OFFCHAIN-011.activation: An operation has an execution-validity deadline; Operators or clients must observe status and may submit evidence later

NA-OFFCHAIN-012.title: Keep documented recovery aligned with implemented states
NA-OFFCHAIN-012.activation: Users or operators depend on recovery instructions; Documentation may describe an obsolete failure branch

NA-AUTH-012.title: Public session credential can be reassigned across owners
NA-AUTH-012.activation: Public credential identifier plus cross-owner registration of a live session
